stories.headline: Peters' 18-pitch walk keys White Sox's win vs. Guardians
stories.summary: White Sox center fielder Tristan Peters' 18-pitch walk proved the turning point in a 7-3 win over the Guardians on Monday that put Chicago in the driver's seat for the AL Central title.
stories.body:
CLEVELAND -- The longest plate appearance in six years might have saved the Chicago White Sox's season.

Center fielder Tristan Peters drew an 18-pitch walk against Guardians ace Gavin Williams in the sixth inning of a scoreless game -- after which Chicago scored six runs. Williams was immediately pulled after throwing a season-high 113 pitches as the final 18 to Peters were the most to a player in MLB since St. Louis Cardinals catcher Matt Wieters faced 19 in 2020.

"It felt like I was up there for an hour," Peters said after a 7-3 win. "I was just exhausted. ... I was just trying to see it as deep as possible, especially when it got to two strikes."

Peters fouled off 12 pitches in the plate appearance, which began with two called strikes after a first-pitch ball.

The White Sox dugout was buzzing after yet another Peters feat this season. The All-Star has already hit for the cycle and tied a rookie record with home runs in five straight games. Now he has added one of the better at-bats of the season to his résumé.

Teammate Andrew Benintendi was on second base during the at-bat.

"I was getting plenty of reps in for my secondary leads," Benintendi said. "Never seen that before. It's easy to get in swing mode. His two [late] takes were unbelievable."

Moments later, Peters made a smart baserunning play by getting into Nathaniel Lowe's throwing lane as he was hit in the helmet while Lowe attempted to get a force out at second. It scored Benintendi with the first run of the game before the White Sox added four more hits, including Miguel Vargas ' 31st home run.

"It's no secret what's on the line here," winning pitcher Sean Burke said. "Everyone is aware of it. That AB by Peters was huge. That's probably the most impressive at-bat I've seen this year in the league."

Manager Will Venable added: "Once you get to eight to nine pitches, there is a buzz in the dugout."

The big inning came after Williams kept getting in and out of trouble early. The White Sox were 0-for-7 with runners in scoring position in the first four innings, a frustrating trend that has plagued them throughout a mediocre run at the plate lately. It has led to a tightening in the AL Central as the Guardians came into the game just a half-game behind the first-place White Sox.

"That was more like ourselves," Peters said of the offensive output. "It just felt like the baseball we play."

Not only did the win extend the lead in the division, it clinched the tiebreaker over Cleveland for Chicago -- which has won seven of the first 11 games between the two teams. According to ESPN Analytics, the White Sox have a 77% chance to win the AL Central. That would have dropped to 44% with a loss Monday.

Though the White Sox got great pitching from both Burke and opener Sean Newcomb, Peters' long plate appearance was the topic of conversation postgame. He was asked what he thought about seeing the most pitches in an at-bat since the beginning of the decade.

"I think it's really funny," he said. "Really random. I would never have expected that. I think I swung at one that may have hit me. You're just in fight mode there."

stories.headline: Kenneth Walker III's dazzling debut leads Chiefs over Broncos
stories.summary: Making his Chiefs debut, Kenneth Walker III powered Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs past the Broncos on "Monday Night Football."
stories.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Back on the field inside Arrowhead Stadium for the first time in nine months, quarterback Patrick Mahomes wasn't the biggest star -- or the biggest difference-maker -- in the Kansas City Chiefs' resounding 31-10 win Monday night over the AFC West rival Denver Broncos.

Running back Kenneth Walker III, the reigning Super Bowl MVP who joined the Chiefs in March, was stellar in his Kansas City debut.

Monday's outcome was exactly what the Chiefs wanted from their offense, as Walker's speed and ball-carrying abilities took much of the burden off Mahomes, who made his much-anticipated return from the surgery that repaired the torn ACL and LCL in his left knee, an injury that occurred Dec. 14. In 26 touches, in a variety of ways, Walker ran through, around and past the Broncos for an outstanding performance, finishing with 191 all-purpose yards and two touchdowns.

Walker converted on four short-yardage situations, including a 60-yard touchdown on fourth-and-inches early in the third quarter. He became just the third player since 2000 with least 100 rushing yards in his Chiefs debut, joining running back Kareem Hunt (148 yards in 2017) and Clyde Edwards-Helaire (138 yards in 2020), according to ESPN Research.

The Broncos never led and were never able to get quarterback Bo Nix into rhythm.

Nix, who also was returning after having two offseason surgeries to repair his fractured right ankle -- which forced him to miss last season's AFC Championship Game -- struggled throughout, including throwing an interception on the Broncos' opening drive. The Chiefs sacked Nix four times, and speedy receiver Jaylen Waddle, one of Denver's biggest offseason acquisitions, was limited to just one reception for 2 yards.

Here are the most important things to know for both teams:

Kansas City Chiefs

What to make of the QB performance: Mahomes wasn't perfect, but he didn't need to be to beat the Broncos. The Chiefs' opening drive demonstrated Mahomes' toughness and impressive speed when he scrambled out of the pocket inside the red zone to score a 15-yard touchdown. Mahomes' top speed on his highlight was 15.8 mph, which was 2.5 mph faster than his average speed on rushing attempts last season, according to Next Gen Stats. In the second half, Mahomes improved his passing rhythm to finish with 184 yards and two touchdown passes.

Most surprising performance: The Chiefs' defense dominated the Broncos, doing so with the help of an influx of rookies. Cornerback Mansoor Delane, the sixth pick, intercepted Nix to set up the Chiefs' first touchdown. Defensive end R Mason Thomas finished with a sack, and defensive tackle Peter Woods generated pressure on passing downs. Even cornerback Nohl Williams, a second-year player, did an excellent job in coverage against receiver Courtland Sutton, who finished with just two receptions for 11 yards.

Next game: vs. Indianapolis Colts (Sunday, Sept. 20, at 8:20 p.m. ET)

Denver Broncos

The Broncos spent an offseason outlining just how much they needed an improved run game and new wide receiver Jaylen Waddle.

And then they spent their opening night of the season with little action from either. Denver ran the ball just 12 times in the game.

Waddle, who did show his potential impact on Evan Engram's touchdown catch in the first quarter when several Chiefs defenders leaned toward Waddle as Engram ran free, had one catch for 2 yards when the game was still in the balance.

This was not the debut the Broncos wanted. They're still searching for that improved run game -- and for Waddle to be a big part of the offense.

Most surprising performance: On a night the Broncos held Mahomes to 15-of-27 passing, Walker did the most damage. He romped for a 60-yard touchdown on Kansas City's fourth play of the second half, giving him 149 yards on 16 carries to that point, leaving a pile of missed tackles in his wake. Walker finished with 173 yards to go with a rushing TD and a receiving TD, more rushing yards than any back had against the Broncos in all of 2025.

What to make of the QB performance: Nix showed some quick bounce-back ability early. After he took a sack and threw an interception in the first and third plays from scrimmage, respectively, he went 5-for-5 on a touchdown drive in the Broncos' next possession. But overall, he, like the rest of the Broncos' offense, looked out of sorts. Nix fumbled three times, losing one, and threw an interception. It was just the third lost fumble for Nix in his career, with one of those being in last season's opener.

Trend to watch: Running back J.K. Dobbins was one of the league's rushing leaders when he suffered a season-ending foot injury in a Week 10 win over the Raiders last November. Coach Sean Payton said re-signing Dobbins in the offseason was one of the team's highest priorities because the Broncos had big plans for the 27-year-old back. One game does not a season make, but in offensive coordinator Davis Webb's first regular-season game as a playcaller, Dobbins had just three carries in the first half and the Broncos were down two scores before Dobbins got carries on consecutive plays.

Stat of note: While Payton has called Nix's ability to be "hard to sack'' one of the quarterback's superpowers, the Chiefs sacked Nix four times Monday. Nix was sacked more than twice in only two games last season -- three by the Raiders and four by the Chargers in the regular-season finale.

Next game: vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (Sunday, Sept. 20, at 4:05 p.m. ET)

stories.headline: Source: Colombia, U.S. battling for Inter Miami U20 dual national Alexander Shaw
stories.summary: Inter Miami midfielder Alexander Shaw has been contacted by Colombia after playing for the United States U-20 team in the 2026 Concacaf tournament, a source confirmed to ESPN.
stories.body:
Inter Miami midfielder Alexander Shaw is currently being pursued by both Colombia and the United States on a youth Under 20 level, a source confirmed to ESPN.

He previously featured for the United States youth national team in the 2026 Concacaf U20 champion, reaching the final after a perfect group stage. Shaw helped the USYNT to victories against Haiti, El Salvador and Cuba without conceding a goal.

Shaw scored in the 5-0 victory over Cuba.

The USYNT concluded the tournament as runners-up after falling 2-0 to Mexico.

Shaw has previously received call ups from the Colombia U20, but a source confirms that all requests have been declined by Inter Miami for occurring during Major League Soccer regular season action.

Shaw, however, joined the Colombian national team during the World Cup as a sparring under manager Nestor Lorenzo while the squad trained in Miami.

A source confirmed to ESPN that both Colombia and the United States are looking for Shaw to join the team for the upcoming U-20 World Cup in 2027.

Inter Miami recently signed Shaw to a contract through the end of the 2026 MLS season, with options to extend through June 2027, the 2027-28 and 2028-29 seasons.

He's made five appearances this season and recorded a goal in the 7-1 victory over CF Montreal.

stories.headline: Mikel Arteta promises Max Dowman minutes this season but warns they must be earned
stories.summary: Mikel Arteta has insisted Arsenal starlet Max Dowman will get minutes this season but warned they must be earned ahead of Tuesday's Carabao Cup fourth-round tie at Ipswich.
stories.body:
Mikel Arteta has insisted Arsenal starlet Max Dowman will get minutes this season but warned they must be earned ahead of Tuesday's Carabao Cup fourth-round tie at Ipswich.

Arsenal finished as runners-up in the competition last season after they lost at Wembley to Manchester City and head to Suffolk for a tricky all Premier League tie eager to make it five victories from five for the new campaign.

Arsenal's 16-year-old sensation Dowman has been an unused substitute on four occasions for Arsenal this season, most recently at Napoli last Wednesday, but has topped up his game time with a handful of runouts for the under-21s and featured in a 4-1 loss to Chelsea at the weekend.

Last season Dowman became the youngest player to start a Premier League fixture when he was given the nod at Crystal Palace and produced a memorable cameo against Everton where he scored his first professional goal in stunning fashion.

However, with Arteta able to name Noni Madueke, Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyökeres on the bench during a 2-0 win at Sunderland on Saturday, the Spaniard could not guarantee Dowman would start at Portman Road on Tuesday.

"Well, I wish we could have him here [at Sunderland], but we have a limitation with the numbers we have," Arteta said in his latest remark about the Premier League rule of 20 players in a matchday squad.

"Max will have his chance. He will have his minutes and he will have to earn them like anybody else.

"You know the talent that we have, the players that we have there, we need to help him and find a way to make sure he continues to develop."

- Roberto De Zerbi leaves Richarlison out of Spurs' Carabao Cup squad for Liverpool clash

- Arsenal to contact Pro Ref over Sunderland penalty incident - source

- Ex-Man United striker Wayne Rooney: 'Baffling' that VAR awarded Erling Haaland goal

Dowman will hope to earn a first senior appearance of the campaign at Ipswich and Arteta promised there would be no shortage of motivation from his Premier League champions.

While the Carabao Cup will presumably be low on the list of priorities for the north London club in comparison to defending their league crown and going for a maiden Champions League win, the 44-year-old knows his squad will relish the change to progress in the competition.

"It's the next game ahead and the next competition," Arteta said.

"We will look at the players eyes, they will say they want to play, they want to win the game, they want to improve and they want to review the [Sunderland] game and they will be willing for me, because I know the boys."

Bukayo Saka scored late on in a hard-fought victory at Sunderland, which occurred after a narrow midweek win at Napoli and after a close battle with London rivals Chelsea.

Tuesday will be Arsenal's third consecutive away match and Saka told the official club website: "It's been a massive week for us.

"There has been a lot of travelling. People don't understand behind the scenes how it's been, but I'm really happy with how we've managed this.

"It's amazing for us, so credit to the team, the staff, all of us. We need to keep going -- it doesn't stop."

stories.headline: 2026 NBA buzz: Latest free agency and trade updates
stories.summary: We're tracking deals, trades and buzz across the NBA, including the latest on Kawhi Leonard and the NBA's investigation into the Clippers.
stories.body:
NBA free agency has almost reached the end, with several players landing in new homes this offseason.

LeBron James decided to continue his historic career with the Philadelphia 76ers after months of deliberation. The Sixers also traded for Jaylen Brown this summer, turning the franchise into a true contender with two huge moves.

Meanwhile, Giannis Antetokounmpo is headed to South Beach to team up with Bam Adebayo and the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers have been sold for the second time in 10 months.

What will happen next during this turbulent offseason?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Sept. 14

Sources: Duren feels 'disrespected' in contract talks
The Detroit Pistons are focused on bringing back restricted free agent Jalen Duren, Andscape's Marc Spears said on "NBA Today," but there are feelings to mend.

"They have some optimism, but it's complicated," Spears said. "I just hear that, for Jalen, it's not about money right now. He feels disrespected. ... There's a black cloud going into camp. ... They gotta try to fix it, and I don't know if they can in time."

Kawhi Leonard trade to Toronto officially confirmed

The trade sending Kawhi Leonard to the Toronto Raptors for Gradey Dick, Brandon Ingram and future draft picks was confirmed Monday, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Taj Gibson officially retires, joins Bulls as assistant coach

Following a 17-year NBA career, Taj Gibson has retired and agreed to return to the Chicago Bulls as an assistant coach under Tiago Splitter, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Sept. 13

Ballmer and Clippers to comply with NBA punishments
Eleven days after the NBA issued punishments stemming from its investigation into the LA Clippers' dealings with Kawhi Leonard, team owner Steve Ballmer issued a statement saying he and the team would comply with them.

Those punishments include a $30 million fine, yearlong suspensions for Ballmer and president of business operations Gillian Zucker, a six-month suspension for president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank, and five lost first-round picks.

Sept. 10

Justice Department opens criminal inquiry into Clippers' dealings with Leonard
The U.S. Justice Department has opened a criminal investigation into the LA Clippers, The New York Times reported Thursday evening, looking at how the team allegedly arranged secret sponsorship contracts for Leonard.

The probe is being conducted by the U.S. attorney's office in Brooklyn, New York.

Sept. 8

Pelicans trade Hawkins to Grizzlies in four-player deal
The New Orleans Pelicans have traded Jordan Hawkins, Micah Peavy, a future second-round pick and a future second-round pick swap to the Memphis Grizzlies for AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Tuesday.

The trade clears roster space for the Pelicans, frees up salary flexibility to sign Bennedict Mathurin to a two-year, $16 million deal, and allows the team to have a look at a young player in Johnson, who was the No. 21 pick in the 2023 NBA draft. Hawkins, a lottery pick at No. 14 in the same draft, now gets dealt by his team prior to his fourth season.

Sept. 4

Ben Simmons signs with Kings on one-year deal
Three-time All-Star Ben Simmons has agreed to a one-year, $3.5 million deal with the Sacramento Kings, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. The deal marks a return to the NBA for Simmons, who sat out the 2025-26 season. Simmons was the No. 1 pick in the 2016 NBA draft.

Sept. 3

Windhorst: Steve Ballmer 'very' angry after NBA penalty
ESPN's Brian Windhorst reported that LA Clippers owner Steve Ballmer is 'very angry' after the penalties handed down to the franchise by the NBA on Sept. 2.

"When you're worth $150 billion and you're angry, and he's very clearly angry, you can't advise him, you can't talk to him," Windhorst said on Get Up. "I'd be stunned if his lawyers didn't advise him, as Shams [Charania] said, to make a plea deal because he should've made a please deal."

Read more: NBA punishes Clippers after Kawhi investigation: Top questions​

Thompson, Rockets agree to five-year contract extension
The Houston Rockets and Amen Thompson have agreed to a five-year, $208 million rookie-scale contract extension, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania The deal includes a 10% trade kicker.

Sept. 2

NBA insiders answer the biggest questions on NBA's Clippers investigation
After the NBA released the findings of its yearlong investigation into allegations that the LA Clippers circumvented the salary cap in order to funnel money to Kawhi Leonard, ESPN NBA insiders Baxter Holmes, Brian Windhorst, Ramona Shelburne and Bobby Marks examined the report, the massive punishments the NBA leveled and how all of it could impact this season -- and beyond.

The punishment was compounded by the Clippers being previous offenders during Steve Ballmer's tenure as owner. They were fined $250,000 for a similar accusation involving DeAndre Jordan in 2015. There also was a 2019 investigation into Leonard's signing in which the Clippers were cleared of wrongdoing but subsequently warned and put through a seminar to remind them of the rules.
This penalty is indeed harsh, but it could have been worse.

In the case of Joe Smith and the Minnesota Timberwolves in 2000, his contract was voided and his Bird rights were vacated.

Leonard will have to write a sizable check -- $700,000 -- but he will not be suspended, and his contract and Bird rights remain unaffected.

The Clippers and the Toronto Raptors will be allowed to move forward in their trade process, one league source said. If the trade moves forward, LA will acquire two first-round picks in the deal. -- Windhorst

Read the full story here.

Charania: NBA rules on Kawhi Leonard-Aspiration investigation
Sources told ESPN's Shams Charania reported that, after a year-long probe into Kawhi Leonard-Aspiration connection, the NBA has stripped the LA Clippers of five first-round picks and issued a $30 million fine to owner Steve Ballmer, as well as suspended Ballmer, Lawrence Frank and Gillian Zucker.

On top of that, Leonard will have to pay $700,000 in restitution for improper benefits by the franchise for his uncle and former business representative, Dennis Robertson. Leonard will not be suspended but Robertson is banned by the NBA from all business dealings.

SEC requesting information from Daktronics regarding Clippers probe
The Securities and Exchange Commission is seeking information from Daktronics, the company that designed the LA Clippers' videoboard inside the Intuit Dome, related to Kawhi Leonard, a company executive said Wednesday.

"Let me now briefly address a matter that has been in the media concerning the NBA's investigation of Kawhi Leonard and the Clippers in connection with the league's collective bargaining agreement that many of you may have heard about," chief financial officer Howard Atkins said on Daktronics' quarterly earnings call.

"As you might expect, we have received requests for information from the NBA. Additionally, the Securities and Exchange Commission is seeking information from us concerning the company and Mr. Leonard. "We take these requests seriously and are cooperating. At this point, out of respect for the respective processes, we will not be providing further comment."

A spokesperson for the SEC declined to comment.

Podcaster Pablo Torre reported last month that Daktronics had an undisclosed sponsorship agreement allegedly worth millions of dollars with Leonard.

Torre interviewed someone identified as an "anonymous high-level source under contract for Intuit Dome" who alleged that the sponsorship deal "was 1,000% a way to circumvent the salary cap. It was funneling money from the Clippers through Daktronics back to Kawhi."

The NBA launched its investigation into the Clippers and Leonard last September after numerous podcasts from Torre, who cited internal documents that showed that Clippers owner Steve Ballmer invested $50 million in Aspiration, a now-defunct green banking company, through his personal LLC in September 2021.

That month, the Clippers signed a 23-year, $300 million deal with Aspiration, making the company the "first founding partner" of the Intuit Dome.

Six months later, Aspiration signed its $28 million endorsement deal with Leonard.

An unnamed employee who purportedly worked for the banking company told Torre that Leonard's sponsorship deal "was to circumvent the salary cap."

The Clippers have repeatedly denied that they funneled money through Aspiration to compensate Leonard.

On Aug. 17, ESPN reported that the NBA has found no evidence showing Ballmer funneled money through team sponsors to pay Leonard in order to circumvent the salary cap, per three people with knowledge of recent discussions between the two sides. -- Baxter Holmes

Sept. 1

Windhorst: Sabonis hired new agent this summer, could want out of Sacramento

On the Sept. 1 episode of "The Hoop Collective," ESPN's Brian Windhorst discussed what Domantas Sabonis hiring a new agent this summer could mean for his future with the Sacramento Kings.

Windhorst on Sabonis hiring a new agent: " I do think it's somewhat interesting that he changed agents this offseason. He hired Aaron Mintz of CAA. Steve Heumann and that group. One of the top executives at CAA. This last year, Mintz and his group executed the trade for Trae Young away from Atlanta, executed the trade for Walker Kessler away from the [Jazz]. Domantas Sabonis just hired him.

"At the risk of ... parodying myself from the season, why would he do that?"

Aug. 29

Latest on Curry's next deal decision

The window for Stephen Curry to sign an extension has officially opened.

The four-time champion and two-time MVP is now eligible (through June 30) to sign a two-year, $136.7 million extension. If he signs, Curry will become the first player in NBA history to rack up more than $600 million in on-court earnings.

A new contract for Curry will have important financial implications for Golden State. With Curry, Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III able to become free agents after the 2026-27 season, Golden State could have significant cap space to reshape its roster.

If Curry signs for the maximum allowed in the first season of an extension ($65.7 million), the Warriors project to have between $45 million and $60 million in cap space next offseason. -- Bobby Marks

Wolves, Jazz swap forwards
The Minnesota Timberwolves are trading forward Josh Green to the Utah Jazz for forwards Cody Williams and John Konchar, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

The Wolves are expected to keep Williams, the No. 10 pick in 2024, and waive-and-stretch Konchar, sources said. By moving Green's $14.7 million salary, Minnesota can sign Jonathan Kuminga to the taxpayer midlevel exception.

Aug. 27

Free agent center Richards agrees to one-year deal with Heat
Free agent center Nick Richards has agreed to a one-year deal with the Miami Heat, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. After signing Klay Thompson, the Heat fill roster slot No. 14 with a reserve big man.

Aug. 26

Kuminga signs two-year deal with Minnesota
Free agent forward Jonathan Kuminga agreed to a two-year, $12.4 million deal with the Minnesota Timberwolves, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Kuminga probably will start alongside Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball, Jaden McDaniels and Rudy Gobert.

Mathurin to sign with Pels
Free agent guard Bennedict Mathurin agreed to a two-year, $16 million deal with the New Orleans Pelicans, including a player option, sources tell ESPN.

Aug. 25

Warriors agree to deal with Niang

Forward Georges Niang agreed to a one-year, $3.9 million deal with the Golden State Warriors, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Warriors sign guard Williams
Free agent guard Brandon Williams is signing a one-year, $2.6M deal with the Golden State Warriors, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Williams averaged 13 points and 3.9 assists per game last season for the Dallas Mavericks.

Aug. 24

Blazers lose Sharpe to injury
Portland Trail Blazers guard Shaedon Sharpe sustained a torn meniscus in his right knee, and he is expected to miss six months, sources told ESPN.

Sharpe, 23, averaged 20.8 points for the Blazers last season but missed a large chunk of the campaign with a stress fracture of his left fibula.

His four-year, $90 million extension, which he signed last year, officially kicks in this season. Sharpe will make $20.1 million in 2026-27.

Aug. 21

Nuggets signing DeRozan to one-year deal
Six-time NBA All-Star DeMar DeRozan agreed to sign with the Denver Nuggets on a one-year, $3.9 million deal, sources told ESPN on Friday.

DeRozan landed on the Nuggets after speaking to the Miami Heat, Washington Wizards and New Orleans Pelicans during free agency, choosing a significant role in Denver and a chance to compete in the West. The Nuggets' front office and coaches made a strong recruitment effort in recent weeks to secure DeRozan's commitment, showing him how he would complement Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray as an additional playmaker. He also gives the Nuggets a veteran backcourt presence after sending young, versatile wing Peyton Watson to Cleveland as part of a four-team trade.

Mavs buy out Thompson, to sign with Heat
Klay Thompson is expected to sign with the Miami Heat after clearing waivers following his contract buyout from the Dallas Mavericks, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Friday.

Thompson, 36, was due to make $17.5 million in the final season of his contract with the Mavericks, who announced his buyout Friday afternoon.

He played two seasons for the Mavericks, averaging 12.9 points per game and shooting 38.7% from 3-point range. Thompson passed Damian Lillard last season to rank fourth in career 3-pointers made.

Aug. 20

Harden to return to Cavs
Free agent James Harden agreed to sign a three-year, $97M contract to return to the Cleveland Cavaliers, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania, with a player option for the 2028-29 season.

The Cavs acquired Harden, who turns 37 on Aug. 26, from the LA Clippers in early February in a trade for guard Darius Garland. Cleveland went 21-9 after Harden debuted, tied for the fifth-best record after Feb. 7, as he averaged 20.5 points, 7.7 assists and 4.8 rebounds per game after the All-Star break.

Aug. 19

Watson to Cavs in multiteam trade
The Cleveland Cavaliers, Denver Nuggets and LA Clippers agreed on a trade sending Peyton Watson to the Cavaliers, Max Strus to LA, and an unprotected 2031 Cavs first-round pick and 2032 Sacramento Kings second-rounder to the Nuggets, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. As part of the trade, the Cavaliers will send Tre Mann to the Washington Wizards for Cam Whitmore and a 2027 second-round pick.

Watson will sign a new four-year, $88 million deal with Cleveland.

Aug. 17

Suns, Highsmith agree to one-year deal

The Phoenix Suns and forward Haywood Highsmith agreed to a one-year deal, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Watford, Pelicans agree to one-year deal
Free agent forward Trendon Watford agreed to a one-year, $2.9 million deal with the New Orleans Pelicans, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Watford, 25, considered multiple options, but for New Orleans he serves as a productive two-way get late into the offseason.

Aug. 14

Cavaliers trade Schroder, cash to Hornets for Mann
The Cleveland Cavaliers are trading Dennis Schroder and cash to the Charlotte Hornets for Tre Mann, sources told ESPN on Friday.

The Hornets, Cavaliers and Schroder's rep, Mark Bartelstein of Priority Sports, worked for the past couple months on the deal, which also provides Cleveland flexibility to continue pursuing roster moves and tax savings to keep the team well under the second apron, according to ESPN's Bobby Marks.

Aug. 13

Why Dolan is so worried about the second apron
The New York Knicks' championship parade has not even started, but there are already questions over whether finances will break up the roster.

"If we could bring back the whole team, exactly as is, why wouldn't you?" Knicks owner James Dolan said Wednesday on WFAN's "Carton Show." "I don't know if we'll be able to.

"We're willing to stretch, but there's certain things in the NBA that you'd have to be suicidal to do. One of them is the second apron. Cannot go into the second apron."

Including the 24th pick in next week's draft (June 23 and 24, 8 p.m. ET on ABC/ESPN), New York is $13 million below the second apron and has decisions with free agents Landry Shamet, Mitchell Robinson and possibly Jose Alvarado. (Alvarado has until Monday to decide on his $4.5 million option.) The entire starting five, meanwhile, is under contract through at least 2026-27. Karl-Anthony Towns is extension-eligible this summer and can become a free agent in the 2027 offseason if an agreement is not reached.

The second apron is a punitive luxury tax threshold restricting how teams add to their rosters in free agency, trades and the draft. In the case of the Knicks, the team would not be allowed to send cash in a trade, use the $6.1 million tax midlevel exception, aggregate salaries in a trade or use more than 100% of the traded player exception.

A team cannot trade its first-round pick seven years out if it finishes over the second apron in consecutive seasons, which no team has ever done. That same pick could be moved back to the end of the first round if a team finishes over the second apron in three out of four seasons. Luckily for Dolan and the Knicks, there are no rules that prohibit a team from retaining its own players.

New York can exceed the threshold to sign Robinson, Shamet and Alvarado. If the Knicks let the three players sign elsewhere, they would have their first-round pick (New York also has the 31st and 55th picks in the second round), the $6.1 million tax midlevel exception and $2.5 million veteran minimum exceptions available as replacements.

Since the apron rules were implemented before the 2024-25 season, Cleveland, Phoenix, Minnesota and Boston have finished the regular season over the second apron. The Knicks finished the past two seasons $53,000 and $370,000 below. Next offseason, New York is projected to be $31 million below the second apron with seven players under contract. -- Bobby Marks

The Minnesota Timberwolves won the battle on Saturday night, with a stirring Game 4 victory over Denver that brought the team within a win of the second round.

But they might have lost the war.

On Saturday night, ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Donte DiVincenzo had torn his right Achilles and would miss the rest of the postseason. And on Sunday morning, he reported that four-time All-Star Anthony Edwards would miss multiple weeks after hyperextending his left knee.

Losing a starting backcourt in one fell swoop would hurt any team in the playoffs, but it should be especially tough on Minnesota. The Timberwolves rely on a strong core, with little depth behind it; entering Saturday's games, only seven Wolves had averaged more than 10 minutes per game in the playoffs. By comparison, 10 members for both the Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs played more than that, and even the injury-riddled Lakers had eight.

With Edwards and DiVincenzo out, Minnesota's entire rotation and offensive gameplan will shift. Ayo Dosunmu -- fresh off a 43-point outburst -- and Bones Hyland are the likely replacement starters, with some combination of Mike Conley, Terrence Shannon Jr. (who received his first playoff minutes in Game 4) and Kyle Anderson receiving more minutes off the bench.

That might not be a tenable arrangement on offense, unless Dosunmu can continue posting career highs in points going forward. There's very little shooting and playmaking talent left in Minnesota's lineup, and Julius Randle -- who has been only OK against Denver, averaging 17.5 points and 3.5 assists per game on subpar efficiency -- will need to step up in Edwards' stead.

But all isn't lost for the Timberwolves, at least against the Nuggets. Surprisingly, lineups without DiVincenzo and Edwards held their own in the regular season, with a plus-3.0 net rating, per Cleaning the Glass (which removes garbage time). Those groups excelled on defense. And as long as Rudy Gobert and Jaden McDaniels remain on the floor, Minnesota will retain its top two options to guard Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray, respectively.

Minnesota is already winning because of its defense. The Timberwolves have a 112.3 offensive rating in the playoffs, which is worse than their regular-season mark (115.6). That's because one quirk of the tournament's addition is that, not unlike the NBA Cup title game, the play-in tournament lives as its own statistical entity. They are neither playoff nor regular-season games, with no bearing on postseason and regular-season stats or awards.

stories.headline: Source: Avalanche's Joe Sakic to stay on as GM indefinitely
stories.summary: Avalanche president of hockey operations Joe Sakic will also remain general manager indefinitely with no GM search scheduled, a source told The Associated Press on Monday.
stories.body:
CASTLE ROCK, Colo. -- Joe Sakic will remain in the role of general manager for the Colorado Avalanche indefinitely with no search scheduled, a person with knowledge of the situation told The Associated Press on Monday.

Already the president of hockey operations, Sakic added the title of GM in June when the Nashville Predators hired away Chris MacFarland to lead their front office. The person spoke of Sakic's dual responsibilities on condition of anonymity because the team hasn't announced the decision.

Sakic was the architect behind building the Avalanche squad that captured the 2022 Stanley Cup title. He turned the responsibilities over to MacFarland soon after the celebratory parade that summer. It's a position MacFarland held until the Predators made him their president of hockey operations/general manager.

As a player, Sakic led the Avalanche to Stanley Cup titles in 1996 -- their first season in Denver -- and 2001. The Hall of Fame forward is the only one in league history to win a title as a captain and GM with the same franchise.

It has been a busy offseason for Sakic that has included several trades with MacFarland (Ross Colton was sent to the Predators, and later so was Jack Drury).

Sakic created quite a bit of buzz around the league in late August by making standout defenseman Cale Makar the highest paid player in NHL history. Makar, a two-time Norris Trophy winner, signed a $163.2 million, eight-year extension that kicks in next season. As a way to free up space to negotiate the extension, Sakic dealt Valeri Nichushkin to the Columbus Blue Jackets for draft picks.

Colorado is coming off a season in which the team won the Presidents' Trophy with the best record in hockey before being swept by Vegas in the Western Conference final. Among the moves made by Sakic was bringing in forward Jaden Schwartz on a three-year contract. Schwartz had 11 goals and 15 assists over 50 games with the Seattle Kraken last season.

The Avalanche assembled Monday for a charity golf tournament. They start training camp later this week.

"A very talented group," Schwartz said of the Avalanche before teeing off. "They're a team that's been up there in the standings every year and have a good chance every year. I feel pretty fortunate to be part of it now."

stories.headline: Max vs 100 explained: Rules, drivers, shortcuts and how Verstappen can win
stories.summary: Everything you need to know ahead of Max v 100 at Silverstone, as Max Verstappen takes on a unique new challenge.
stories.body:
In one of the most unique challenges ever faced by a Formula One driver, Max Verstappen is taking to Silverstone on Wednesday, where he will try to overtake 100 drivers in just 30 laps.

Verstappen first sat in a kart at the age of four and was taking part in competition by the age of seven -- but has been in Formula 1 for the past 11 years.

He's set to roll back the years and test his go-karting pedigree once more against drivers from the world of social media, TV and sport.

Here's everything you need to know about Max vs 100.

- Max vs 100: Meet the drivers racing against Red Bull's Verstappen

- Max vs 100: F1 drivers predict how Verstappen will fare racing 100 drivers

- What makes Max Verstappen so good? Career, background and F1 records

What is Max vs 100?
Max vs 100 is a one-off go-kart race organised by Red Bull, which sees four-time Formula 1 world champion Max Verstappen attempt to beat 100 amateur drivers from around the world at Silverstone.

What does Verstappen have to do to win?
Verstappen will start from the back of the grid, with all 100 competitors ahead of him. He will have 30 laps to overtake all of them in order to win.

When a kart is overtaken by Verstappen, they are out, meaning Verstappen could win before the 30 laps are complete.

What is the 'fast lap' and how do the shortcuts work?
Anyone attempting to hold off one of the greatest Formula 1 drivers of all time will need a little bit of help, and Max vs 100 competitors will have access to a 'fast lap' once during the race.

Drivers will be able to use their 'fast lap' at any time in the first 15 laps of the race, which will enable to them to take a shortcut on the track and gain some ground back on Verstappen when he begins to close in.

However, Verstappen has one available of his own to gain time -- but he cannot use it until the last 15 laps.

How does qualifying work?
The grid order will be determined by one flying lap around the specially-designed course at Silverstone -- with just a single attempt available. Much like in Formula 1, the grid order will be determined by lap times.

Are all the karts the same?
Every kart is identical. The complete weight, including driver and kit, must reach 85kg, meaning ballast will be added to karts which do not reach the total, levelling out the field.

Who are the 100 drivers facing Verstappen?
Among the drivers taking on Verstappen are personalities from TV, social media, and sport, though no professional racing drivers are included.

The list includes streamers Pieface, Caedrel and TheDonato, ultrarunner Arda Saatçi, basketball shooting phenomenon Chris "Lethal Shooter" Matthews, and 2019 Love Island winner Amber Gill.

Verstappen will be able to communicate with the field directly during the race, offering an insight into his racing brain.

How difficult will Max vs 100 be?
Verstappen's challenge in this race will not be in terms of raw pace or lap times, where he is certain to be a cut above the rest.

The issues will come in the form of traffic -- with so many karts ahead of him and some very likely to be lapped -- and time management, as Verstappen will need to calculate where and when he is to attempt passes.

A few of the field, while not professional, are karting influencers who know how to get round a track, and will want to make the most of their opportunity to defend against a Formula 1 icon.

When and how do I watch it?
Max vs 100 is taking place on Sept. 16, and will be shown live in the UK on Disney+.

In the U.S., Max v 100 will also air on the ESPN App for Unlimited subscribers before a delayed ESPN2 broadcast later that day.

The race itself will start at 6 p.m., with the live stream beginning one hour before.

Comedian Mo Gilligan will front the coverage, which is set to include drone footage and live race data.

stories.headline: Tom Aspinall vacates UFC heavyweight title amid ongoing eye issues
stories.summary: Tom Aspinall has decided to vacate his UFC heavyweight title as a result of "ongoing complications" with injuries to his eyes.
stories.body:
Tom Aspinall has decided to vacate his UFC heavyweight title as a result of "ongoing complications" with injuries to his eyes.

The Brit confirmed his decision via a statement on social media on Monday, saying he was "gutted." Aspinall (15-3) said he had been back sparring and had a new fight date locked in, but an accident in training has brought a further set-back.

Aspinall has not fought since his no contest against Ciryl Gane last October, when he was poked in the eyes. He was forced to retire from the fight in the first round and has since had multiple surgeries in both his eyes.

"Ongoing complications with my eyes mean I cannot get medically cleared to fight right now," Aspinall said.

"I've had multiple surgeries, accidents and infections, and done everything possible to get back to competing.

"I had previously agreed to a fight date and was back sparring, feeling great and ready to compete when an accident caused further damage to my right eye. This means more time away from the sport, and right now, the timing of my return is unclear.

"I've now made the decision to vacate the heavyweight title. I've asked the UFC to allow me to make this statement because I don't want to hold the heavyweight division up. I know what it's like to have your career put on hold and I want the other fighters to have the opportunity to compete for the title."

In June, Aspinall confirmed he was back in full training and working towards a rematch with Gane, who beat Alex Pereira that month.

Following Gane's win over Pereira, Aspinall said on his YouTube channel that the was ready for a rematch with the Frenchman and prepared to fight in Paris.

Aspinall stressed he wanted to return to action as soon as possible but on the advice of doctors, would not be fighting in the foreseeable future.

"We have worked closely with different doctors and specialists to try and make my return happen, but unfortunately, it's simply not possible right now," he said. "I'm absolutely gutted. I've chased this dream since I was 10 years old.

"I'm not done. Stepping away from the title is not stepping away from the sport or the dream. I'll continue doing everything I can to get healthy, get cleared and get back to competing as soon as possible."

stories.headline: U.S. beats France for fifth straight women's World Cup title
stories.summary: Team USA largely credited Breanna Stewart for helping guide them to the program's fifth straight World Cup title after a win over France in the final.
stories.body:
BERLIN -- For the first time in years, maybe decades, Team USA looked vulnerable entering and even during the 2026 women's basketball World Cup.

Veterans A'ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum were late scratches heading into the tournament. France, which nearly beat the U.S. at the Olympics in 2024, was out for blood. A three-point win against Italy in the group phase and a close call against Spain in the semifinals only made the outside noise intensify heading into Sunday's gold medal match.

The feeling was that maybe Team USA would miss out on gold at a major international tournament for the first time since 2006 and only the second time since 1994.

But as team captain Breanna Stewart sat in the news conference following Saturday's semifinal, previewing the final showdown against France, she exuded a quiet confidence.

"I've been in these games," she said at the time. "The emotional part of it is really what's going to teeter teams [for things] to not go their way. And my team, we're going to be locked in. We're going to be very composed. Doesn't matter what happens to us, we know that it's going to be a long game."

About 24 hours later, Stewart sat back in that very spot with an American flag draped around her and a gold medal around her neck, fresh off leading USA to a 97-79 victory over France. Her 22-point, 10-rebound performance in the final helped her earn World Cup MVP honors.

"I pride myself on being consistent, and that's showing up when it's the big moments and the small moments and all the moments in between," Stewart said. "It's like an unrealistic confidence that I have in myself, especially in those big moments. I believe that I always have a chance to win no matter what happens in the game."

Stewart further solidified her argument as arguably the winningest player in the sport's history, boasting four NCAA championships, three WNBA titles, three Olympic gold medals and now four World Cup golds, tying Sue Bird for the most of all time.

"It starts with Stewie," coach Kara Lawson said. "Her leadership, not just tonight, throughout the whole tournament, helping to guide the younger players, talk to them, just show them what it looks like to win.

"She is USA Basketball. When you think of the last 15 years, it's Stewie, and we're just really lucky to be a part of her era of this group."

Stewart has been a stalwart with USA Basketball for over a decade and in recent years has taken the reins alongside Wilson as pillars of this era of Team USA. But her on-court productivity and leadership had never been more important than in Berlin. The team was left with just three players -- Stewart, Chelsea Gray and Kahleah Copper -- who'd played in a World Cup before, a tournament many say is harder to win than the Olympics. Seven of the 12 had never even suited up for the senior national team in a major tournament.

Stewart ultimately led Team USA in scoring (12.8 points per game), rebounds (7.3 RPG) and efficiency rating (18.8), anchoring the defense and often even playing point guard if that's what the game required. She had her fingerprints all over the France win between a crucial 12 points in the first half to keep the USA afloat and timely plays that helped the team pull away after halftime.

"The thing that I appreciate about her the most is her willingness to do anything to help the team," Lawson said. "It's so rare in a player of her caliber.

"She will play any position for us to win, and that quality is why she's the greatest winner that we've had, probably."

Her most important contribution might have come off the court. She was the standard-bearer tasked with ensuring that this younger generation understands the expectations that come with representing the U.S. And she also had to help them navigate the pressure that comes with that.

In the weight room after the team barely beat Italy in its second game -- in what would have been one of the most shocking results the sport had seen in years -- Stewart noticed several younger players had a look of "what just happened" on their faces. She shared with them how heading into the 2014 World Cup, her first, USA lost to France in an exhibition but still went on to win the tournament.

"Stewie's been a tremendous leader through this whole process for us," Caitlin Clark said after the gold medal game. "Even after we had that close game with Italy, she was somebody that was really vocal in the locker room about, 'Don't be flustered by this. This is normal for a World Cup. You're going to have to kind of get it out of the mud at some points. It's not always going to be pretty.'"

The team's ability to internalize her message and stay the course was crucial for the remainder of the tournament, and perhaps in no situation more than when France jumped ahead by 14 in the second quarter. It was the first double-digit deficit Team USA faced in a World Cup game since the 2006 semifinal, the program's last loss in the event.

"Our group, our starters especially, when we got down big, we didn't crumble under pressure," Stewart said about the team's ability to cut the deficit to two going into halftime and then respond with a 30-12 third quarter. "[France's] run wasn't going to dictate how we were going to play the rest of the game."

Added Clark: "Stewie's a winner. All she ever does is win. She's been in so many of these moments, and when you have somebody like that on your team, it's just a really comforting thing."

Stewart didn't do it all alone -- fellow veterans Chelsea Gray, Young, Copper and Napheesa Collier also came up big against France -- but her peers recognize how special Stewart is.

"She's so skilled, man. I think sometimes you get used to seeing excellence all the time and you get complacent," said Gray, who has faced off against Stewart many times competing for WNBA championships. "You see the way she competes, the way she finishes the ball, the way she brings the team together. Things like this don't happen by accident.

"We've done it together a few times and I'm happy to share the court with her."

Added Paige Bueckers: "To see [her operate] up close and personal, it was definitely eye-opening."

The keys to USA Basketball will eventually be handed over to the likes of Bueckers, Clark, Angel Reese and Aliyah Boston, all of whom have now learned from and won with Stewart.

But as far as she's concerned, Stewart doesn't want to be done with USA Basketball -- and winning on the biggest of stages -- anytime soon.

Asked on the television broadcast if she can run it back with this group at the Olympics in Los Angeles in 2028, Stewart responded, "Oh yeah, see you in L.A.!"

stories.headline: Fenerbahce coach returns to work after resignation confusion
stories.summary: Fenerbahce coach Ismail Kartal returned to his duties on Saturday, contradicting media reports from the day before suggesting his resignation was final.
stories.body:
ISTANBUL -- Fenerbahce coach Ismail Kartal returned to his duties on Saturday, contradicting media reports from the day before suggesting his resignation was final.

Kartal had announced he was quitting his role following Thursday's draw against AS Roma in the Champions League but the club refused to accept his resignation.

Kartal, nevertheless, failed to attend training on Friday ahead of a Superlig game against Gaziantep FK.

However, Fenerbahce released a statement late Friday saying Kartal would resume his duties on Saturday for the Super Lig match against Gaziantep on Monday.

On Saturday, the club's official X account showed photos of him at work.

Kartal had resigned to the surprise of the club and its players in his news conference following the 1-1 draw with Roma to begin the Turkish club's Champions League season.

"First of all, I congratulate my players for carrying out the tasks I assigned for tonight's match to the letter. We played football worthy of the Champions League," the state-run Anadolu Agency quoted Kartal as saying on Thursday. "We could have won the match; we had clear chances. The match ended in a draw, and I am proud of my players."

Kartal continued: "Tonight, I am resigning from my position -- never to return. I extend my heartfelt thanks to my players."

In a separate news conference soon after, club chairman Aziz Yildirim said Fenerbahce fans had hurled a water bottle at Kartal, describing the incident as a reason for the coach's decision. Kartal was also upset by a series of social media posts, Yildirim said.

Yildirim insisted that Kartal's resignation was not accepted and that he would remain at the helm.

"You saw the state Ismail was in. Can a person endure that much distress?" Yildirim said. "They threw a water bottle at Ismail Kartal's head. We saw it. That is why he is upset."

"Ismail Kartal remains in his post," Yildirim added. "I said [to Kartal]: 'You will continue,' and that was that."

Despite reports in Turkey that Fenerbahce official Oguz Cetin later met with Kartal but failed to convince him to stay, Kartal is now set to take charge of the team's fixture against Gaziantep FK on Monday.

Fenerbahce is 11th in the 18-team league.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: NRL Midweek Mail semifinals: Katoa opens up on possible Sharks curtain call
stories.summary: Sione Katoa has opened up about his future at the Cowboys and his finals days at the Sharks, while Nathan Cleary is fighting the clock to be fit for Penrith's prelim.
stories.body:
The NRL rarely stands still.

Between training sessions, media appearances, and behind-the-scenes conversations, new storylines often begin to emerge before the weekend arrives.

Throughout the week, ESPN will be gathering notes, insights, and updates from around the competition heading into the NRL's semifinal week.

Katoa reveals Cowboys appeal

Sione Katoa has revealed North Queensland's attacking style was a major attraction behind his move to the Cowboys in 2027.

After helping eliminate his future club from the finals, Katoa told ESPN he "loves the style of footy" they play, describing it as "free footy" and similar to Cronulla's attack.

Katoa emotional over Sharks farewell

"Tonight might have been the last week, maybe the last game," he told ESPN after scoring a double against North Queensland.

"I'm very happy right now that I get another week with my brothers and play again."

Nathan Cleary is in doubt for Penrith's preliminary final after scans revealed an stress-related bone issue in his foot.

The Panthers will assess and monitor their star halfback over the next fortnight, with their week off providing valuable recovery time.

Cleary has, however, been cleared of any suspension concern after receiving only a Grade 1 Dangerous Contact charge for his incident with Hugo Savala.

stories.headline: Who are the winningest NFL coaches of all time?
stories.summary: From Belichick to Reid, there are many iconic coaches in NFL history. Who has the best career record? Check out the stat breakdown now.
stories.body:
Only four head coaches in NFL history have won 300 career games across the regular season and postseason. Kansas City Chiefs coach Andy Reid was the last to cross the 300-win plateau.

Reid recorded his 300th career victory on Jan. 18, 2025, when his Chiefs defeated the Houston Texans 23-14 in the AFC divisional round.

Reid, who signed a five-year, $100 million extension with the Chiefs in April 2024, entered the 2026 season looking to add to his career win total and close the gap between him and the NFL's all-time winningest head coach, Hall of Famer Don Shula.

Let's take a look at which head coaches have the most career victories in NFL history (including both regular-season and postseason play):

*Active NFL head coach

5. Tom Landry, 270 wins

Landry was the Dallas Cowboys' head coach for an NFL-record 29 years in a row and the team had 20 consecutive winning seasons, which is also a league record. Landry led Dallas to two Super Bowl wins, defeating the Miami Dolphins in Super Bowl VI and the Denver Broncos in Super Bowl XII. He was named the NFL's Coach of the Year in 1966 and the UPI NFL Coach of the Year in 1975. Landry was an innovator, with the 4-3 defense among his creations. He was named to the NFL's 100th Anniversary All-Time Team.

*4. Andy Reid, 308 wins

Reid is the only head coach in NFL history who has won 100 games with two franchises: the Philadelphia Eagles (coaching the team from 1999 through 2012) and the Chiefs (he has coached Kansas City since 2013). He led the Eagles on multiple deep playoff runs, including a Super Bowl in 2004 and three straight conference finals from 2001 to 2003. However, he wasn't able to hoist the Lombardi Trophy until he arrived in Kansas City. He has turned the Chiefs into a juggernaut, winning three Super Bowls. Reid is an offensive mastermind and quarterback whisperer. He'll likely continue to rack up wins moving forward with Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce & Co.

3. George Halas, 324 wins

Halas was a co-founder of the NFL and creator of the Bears. For 10 years, he served as player-coach-executive for the Bears (which is how he earned the nickname "Mr. Everything"). In 1930, he retired as a player and focused on ownership, but he would later return to coach the Bears several times. Halas led the Bears to eight NFL championships, tying Belichick's number of titles. Halas coached the team for 40 years and had just six losing seasons. He helped create the T-formation system and used it to set an NFL record for the biggest blowout in league history: a 73-0 win over the Washington team in the 1940 NFL Championship Game. Halas was selected as the AP's NFL Coach of the Year in 1963 and 1965, and he was named to the NFL's 100th Anniversary All-Time Team.

2. Bill Belichick, 333 wins

Belichick is considered by some as the greatest coach in all of professional sports, as he has won an NFL-record eight Super Bowls (six as a head coach with the Patriots and two as an assistant coach with the Giants). He also ranks first among all NFL coaches in playoff wins with 31. Belichick was named the AP's NFL Coach of the Year in 2003, 2007 and 2010. Many franchises have hired away Belichick's assistants and tried to replicate his "Patriot Way," but it hasn't been the same without him. If Belichick returns to NFL coaching, he is just 26 regular-season wins from surpassing Don Shula as the winningest regular-season coach of all time.

1. Don Shula, 347 wins

After playing in the NFL as a defensive back for seven seasons, Shula decided to retire and become a coach. He got his first head-coaching opportunity in 1963 with the Baltimore Colts, whom he led to the NFL championship in 1968. From 1970 through 1995, Shula had a legendary run as head coach of the Dolphins. Shula led the Dolphins to a pair of Super Bowl victories (in Super Bowl VII and Super Bowl VIII). Miami had a perfect season in 1972, making Shula the only coach in NFL history to go undefeated. He was named the AP's NFL Coach of the Year in 1964, 1967, 1968 and 1972. Whether you're just counting regular-season wins (328) or including playoff wins (347), Shula is the winningest coach in NFL history.

Be sure to check out ESPN's NFL coverage, including scores, standings, stats, schedules, and more.

stories.headline: Messi tracker: Goals, assists, key moments in 2026
stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 36
Goals: 32
Assists: 14

Sep. 12: Inter Miami 2-2 Nashville SC
In a matchup between the two best teams in the Eastern Conference, the action went end to end, with Messi getting on the scoresheet for Miami's second goal off a Rodrigo De Paul assist as he continues to lead the Golden Boot race.

Ultimately, the teams settled for a point apiece, as the hosts failed to close the gap on Nashville at the top of the table.

Sep. 9: Chicago Fire 1-1 Inter Miami

Two or Europe's greatest club players took center stage in one of the United States' most iconic American football stadiums on Wednesday -- and a record crowd came out to watch.

Ex-Bayern Munich and Barcelona star Robert Lewandowski scored a trademark acrobatic goal in the 10th minute to give the Fire an early lead at the NFL home of the Chicago Bears.

But Inter Miami drew level shortly after halftime when Casemiro, another of the game's stars with a long history of playing in Europe before moving to MLS, headed home a Messi cross from a corner kick to make it 1-1.

The assist was Messi's league-leading 13th of the season. He also has league 18 goals and is the first player in MLS history with 30-plus goal contributions in three separate seasons.

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.
